Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Unity Insurance Group Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Unity Insurance Group's Q3 2023 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Jane Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; David Kim, Chief Investment Officer; and Lisa Wong, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Jane Thompson.

Jane Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Unity Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2023. We delivered strong results, driven by our fortress-like capital position and statutory surplus levels, impressive policy retention rates across major product lines, clear premium growth guidance for the coming periods, favorable customer acquisition cost trends, robust net written premiums growth by line of business, and proactive capital deployment plans including acquisitions and new products. We are particularly excited about the initial success of our UnityDrive telematics product and its positive impact on risk selection, retention, and loss ratios in personal auto.

Michael, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Jane. Good morning, everyone. As Jane mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $650 million, or $2.45 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included strong underwriting profitability, elevated net investment income from higher yields, favorable prior-year reserve development, and disciplined growth across our diversified lines. Our combined ratio was 92.8%. Investment income for the quarter was $320 million, reflecting strong performance in our fixed income segment. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with consolidated statutory surplus at $8.7 billion.

Let me expand on that capital foundation first, as it remains a cornerstone of our financial strength and flexibility here at Unity Insurance Group, a leading multi-line property-casualty carrier with meaningful exposure in personal lines, commercial P&C, and specialty risks. We prioritize robust capitalization to support organic growth, navigate market cycles, and pursue accretive opportunities. As of Q3 2023, our consolidated statutory surplus stood at $8.7 billion, up a solid 11% year-over-year from $7.8 billion at year-end 2022. This growth stemmed from our improved combined ratio of 92.8% in the quarter and higher net investment income, boosted by reinvestment yields during the Fed's rate hiking cycle. Our fixed income portfolio, making up 75% of our $25 billion investment assets under SAP, delivered an annualized book return of 4.2% in Q3, up from 3.1% a year ago, thanks to strategic duration extensions amid 2022 rate volatility.

Our risk-based capital position is equally robust, with the consolidated RBC ratio at 428% of company action level—well above our internal 400% target and the NAIC's 200% authorized control level. This puts us in the top quartile among AM Best-rated peers, on par with Chubb's 420%+ and ahead of Travelers' around 380%. By segment, core P&C operations reached 445% RBC, aided by $185 million in favorable prior-year reserve development, mainly in commercial auto and workers' comp. Our specialty segment, covering D&O and cyber, hit 410%, backed by prudent reinsurance against tail risks like the Change Healthcare-style cyber incidents.

Over the past five years, statutory surplus has compounded at a 9% CAGR, beating the industry's 6-7% average per SNL Financial. Even with $450 million in pre-tax catastrophe losses from Hurricane Lee and Midwest derecho events—adding 2.5 points to the combined ratio—surplus grew 3% quarter-over-quarter, or 7% absent cats. Leverage remains low, with surplus-to-total-admitted-assets at 28% versus the peer median of 24%.

Regionally, our U.S. Southeast book, 20% of gross premiums written, strengthened surplus via rate gains post-Hurricane Ian, with Florida homeowners renewals up 18%. California wildfire pressures are managed through a $1.2 billion net retention covered by excess-of-loss towers placing 85% of limits above $500 million per occurrence. Internationally, Bermuda and London added $650 million to surplus, up 15% YoY, driven by E&S growth in a hardening reinsurance market with January 1 rates up 10-15% per Guy Carpenter.

On initiatives, our 2023 reinsurance program features a $2.8 billion property cat tower with 20% higher attachment points and 2-point ceding commission increases, freeing $300 million in collateral. We've issued $400 million in catastrophe bonds via Unity Re—our fourth since 2020—to diversify from traditional reinsurers like Swiss Re. Our ORSA framework includes 1-in-200-year hurricane stress tests keeping RBC above 350%, and AI-driven stochastic modeling identified $150 million in capital credits from optimizations like credit tenant leases at 5.5% yields.

This agility supports a $500 million Q4 share repurchase targeting 2-3% of float, an 8% ordinary dividend hike to $0.85 per share—our 18th straight increase—and bolt-on M&A in the $500-800 million range, like regional commercial platforms to bolster middle-market channels. We're also investing $200 million in tech, such as telematics for personal auto mirroring Progressive's Snapshot and MGA API integrations for E&S.

Turning to top-line momentum, net written premiums grew 13.2% year-over-year to $4.8 billion in the quarter, with nine-month totals at $14.1 billion, up 12.8%. This is our eighth straight quarter of double-digit growth, powered by rate adequacy, new business wins, and 91.5% retention—our five-year high—amid rate hardening in cat-exposed lines and personal lines capacity gaps at peers.

By line: Personal lines surged 15.4% to $2.1 billion, with 8% policy growth and 9.2% average rate hikes. Auto led at 17.8% to $1.3 billion, boosted by Snapshot telematics at 42% penetration—up from 35%—yielding 15% lower loss ratios, plus fintech embeds like Affirm driving 22% bundled growth. Homeowners rose 12.1% to $800 million, with 11.5% rates via RMS climate modeling; we've non-renewed 4% of high-risk coastal policies, lifting attachment to $250 million per event.

Commercial lines advanced 10.2% to $1.6 billion, with 7.8% rates and 12% new business from Apex360 AI platform using satellite data for 48-hour quotes. Property: 8.5% to $900 million, selective in Florida/Gulf but up 14% in Middle America, backed by Swiss Re tower. Workers' comp: 12.7% to $500 million on national accounts and predictive claims analytics for 10.2% rates at 92% retention. General liability/umbrella: 11.3% to $200 million in E&S.

Specialty exploded 21.6% to $1.1 billion on 15-20% market rates per Verisk. D&O: 24.2% to $450 million on M&A/cyber mandates, with $50 million attachments. Cyber: 28.1% to $350 million amid MOVEit/Clop ransomware, with sub-limits and exclusions. Environmental/trade credit: 14.8% to $300 million.

Geographically, U.S. drove 62% of growth at 14.1% to $3.0 billion via Southeast/Midwest. EMEA: 9.8% to $1.2 billion on UK Ogden reforms. Asia-Pacific: 19.3% to $600 million from Australia P&C and HDFC ERGO JV at 1.2 million policies.

This validates our Precision Growth strategy: $150 million in tech like Guidewire Cloud for 70% of book, faster renewals, and 15% cat quota shares to RenaissanceRe. We see FY23 NWP at 12-14%, with Q4 acceleration.

Retention is another profitability pillar. Overall book retention hit 87.2%, up 140 basis points YoY from 85.8% and 60 basis points sequentially from Q1's 86.6%—our 11th straight sequential gain from tech and initiatives, especially amid cat losses, auto inflation, and commercial softening.

By line (95% of premium): Personal auto (38%): 88.5%, up 220 bps YoY/90 bps seq., via 32% telematics penetration (UnityDrive with AI coaching; UBI at 94% retention). Southeast: 91%; California: 85% on wildfire/regulatory issues. Bundling lifts to 92%.

Homeowners/dwelling (25%): 92.1%, flat YoY/up 40 bps seq., with 8.2% renewals and SmartHome IoT at 18% penetration cutting claims 12%. Midwest: 95%; Florida: 87% post-Ian.

Commercial P&C (22%): 84.3%, down 50 bps YoY but up 110 bps seq. amid 5-7% rate declines per AM Best. Account Lifecycle Manager cut SMB churn 15%; middle-market: 86%, large: 82%. Northeast: 88%; Europe (12% intl.): 81%. Hospitality/cyber: 90%.

Life/annuity (10%): 95.4%, up 60 bps; term: 96.5% via digital portals; annuities: 93% on yields. Asia JV: 92%.

Group health/specialty (5%): 89.2%, up 70 bps seq. as trends eased to 6.8%; stop-loss: 91%.

This drove 2.1-point combined ratio improvement to 93.4%—best non-COVID—and 7.2% earned growth ex-rate. Pillars: $250 million in Guidewire/Duck Creek for 90%+ retention by 2026; GLMs with climate/telematics; Customer 360 loyalty at 25% of book.

Customer acquisition costs also trended favorably, underscoring efficiency. Blended CAC for personal lines fell 14% YoY to $218 per policy from $253, third straight double-digit drop from 2021's $289 peak—beating our 10-12% target and industry's 4% rise per SNL amid ad inflation.

By line: Auto: 16% down to $192; telematics CAC $145 vs. $240 traditional. Homeowners: 12% to $265; bundling (42%) cuts 35%. Payback: 9 months from 12; LTV/CAC 4.2x vs. 3.0x industry.

Digital channels now 68% of acquisitions (from 52%), ahead of Geico with better conversions. AI lead scoring on 1.2 billion data points (Snowflake/Google Cloud) lifted conversions 22%; programmatic/CTV at 4.8x ROAS. Embeds with Ford/GM: 15% Q4 auto at <$100 CAC; Zillow/Redfin for home.

Agents (25%): CAC $385, down 8% via portal analytics. Martech stack (Tealium/Braze/Amplitude) ensures 5% incrementality.

Regions: U.S. (82%): 15% down to $205; Southeast/Midwest 18%. California: 8% on Prop 103/insurtechs. Europe (12%): +3% to €285 on GDPR/FCA, but Germany -11%. Asia (6%): 20% to A$280; India WhatsApp <$10.

Targets: sub-$200 CAC, >5x LTV/CAC by 2025; GenAI quoting, Amazon/Uber embeds, ESG products.

Looking forward, consolidated premium growth guidance for FY 2025 is 7-9%, earned 6-8%; Q4 2024 written 6-8% QoQ annualized, on stable cats/retention.

By segment: P&C (62%): 8-10%; commercial (45%): 9-11% on 5.2% rates, 15% E&S construction share. Personal: 6-8% on 28% telematics.

Group life/health (28%): 5-7%; voluntary high-end via Mercer stop-loss.

Specialty/reins (10%): 10-12%; cyber +22% on CrowdStrike outages, parametric with Munich Re.

Regions: U.S. (72%): 7-9%; Southeast/California 9% hikes. Europe (18%): 6-8% on D&O/AI regs. Asia (10%): 9-11%; India micro-insurance 15%, Australia bushfire reins.

Drivers: Prophet AI at 92% accuracy for 4-6% rates/92% combined; 15 million connected policies cut losses 150 bps; post-Midwest Mutual M&A cross-sell 3%; $1.5 billion reins buybacks. Risks: secondary perils, Berkshire casualty pricing; upside from 8-12% reins rates.

Capital deployment builds on $4.2 billion excess above 500% RBC target, up from $3.8 billion. Framework: organic, M&A, returns for 12-14% ROE, 150-200 bps 2025 EPS accretion.

M&A: $800 million-$1.2 billion pipeline. Closed Midwest Specialty Risk MGU ($450 million; $250 million GWP at 95% combined, +$0.15 EPS). CyberShield Analytics ($725 million; AI modeling boosts cyber accuracy 25%, book to $1.8 billion GWP). LOIs: Southeast life/annuity ($300 million), Nordics parametric reinsurer, Asia health aggregator for 15% growth by 2026.

New products: $350 million R&D (up 20%). UniClimate Guard parametric ag/property ($150 million GWP at 85% loss ratios via Planet Labs). UniDrive Auto telematics (18% lower ratios, 5% auto share). UniHealth Virtual stop-loss/telehealth; Europe ESG life.

Tech: GenAI claims at 75% straight-through, expense to 28.5%. Regions: U.S. E&S/cyber; Europe D&O; Asia JVs. Repos $1.1 billion auth ($400 million YTD); dividend to $0.85.

This positions us for 8-10% growth, 10%+ EPS CAGR.

Sarah Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial P&C line. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-powered pricing models and enhanced telematics integration across personal lines.

David Kim: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income and credit tenant leases.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. The floor is now open for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning, team. Can you provide more color on your capital deployment plans, especially the M&A pipeline?

Jane Thompson: Good morning, John. Michael can provide some additional details here.

Michael Chen: Thanks, John. As I outlined, we're committing substantial deployable capital to high-synergy tuck-ins, like the recent Midwest MGU and CyberShield deals, which are already delivering EPS accretion and tech synergies in cyber. Our pipeline targets diversification into life annuities and parametric reins, calibrated for strong ROEs in hardening markets.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of recent catastrophe losses on your retention and combined ratio?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Emily. Despite $450 million in cats impacting the ratio by 2.5 points, retention improved sequentially across lines, thanks to pricing discipline and tech like SmartHome IoT reducing severity. This resilience positions us well.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez: Thanks. What is the expected impact of regulatory changes like California's Prop 103 on your premium growth and CAC trends?

Sarah Patel: Hi Mike. We're navigating those thoughtfully—tempering personal lines growth in California but offsetting with telematics-driven efficiencies that cut CAC 8% there despite scrutiny. Guidance holds firm.

Operator: Our next question is from Laura Bennett with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Laura Bennett: Good morning. On NWP growth by specialty lines, how sustainable is the cyber momentum?

Michael Chen: Morning, Laura. Cyber's 28% surge reflects disciplined structures amid ransomware trends; CyberShield bolsters our modeling for sustained 10-12% specialty growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel: Hi team. Details on policy retention in commercial—any softness from rate declines?

Sarah Patel: Hi Raj. Retention dipped slightly YoY in commercial due to market softening, but sequential gains from our CRM tools and vertical focus like hospitality have stabilized it at healthy levels, supporting underwriting margins.

Operator: Our final question today from Karen Lee with Citi. Please go ahead.

Karen Lee: Good morning. Forward guidance on CAC and how it ties to LTV?

Michael Chen: Morning, Karen. CAC compression to sub-$200 targets LTV/CAC over 5x, fueled by embeds and GenAI personalization—already yielding 4.2x and ROAS lifts.

Operator: Seeing no further questions at this time.

Jane Thompson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Unity Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
